newsitem.title: USA: Compaq comfortable with $1.37/EPS for Q2.
newsitem.headline: Compaq comfortable with $1.37/EPS for Q2.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp chief financial officer Earl Mason said that he is comfortable with Wall Street analysts' estimates of $1.37 per share for the second quarter, saying he feels "very good" about the second quarter.
He also told Reuters that Compaq's first quarter revenues took a hit of about $200 million due to the stronger dollar outside the United States, but he said earnings were not hurt.
"It probably affected revenues by $200 million but it didn't affect earnings at all," Mason said, "Our treasury group does a good job here hedging (in foreign exchange markets)."
Compaq reported first quarter earnings of $1.36 a share.
Mason said second quarter revenue growth "will be fine."

He added that besides the currency impact that hit first quarter revenues, it was a tough comparison quarter. Compaq had a 42 percent sales jump in the first quarter 1996. In the first quarter just reported, Compaq's revenues grew 14.3 percent to $4.8 billion, versus $4.2 billion a year ago.

Mason said that Compaq will continue to use its increasing cash pile to grow the company, but he declined to talk about any specific plans for its cash, which reached $4.7 billion at the end of the first quarter.
"We continue to study lots of different things," he said.
